info.title: MemberSuite REST API
info.description:
The MemberSuite REST API exposes the association management system as one deployable web app per
feature module. Every module shares the conventions below.

### Authentication

All endpoints except `/about` require an `Authorization` header carrying an access token. Requests
without one are rejected with **401**, as are requests whose token lacks the security rights for the
record being touched — check both the token and the user's security settings when you see a 401.

### Tenants

Routes ending in `{tenantid}` are scoped to a single association. The tenant id is the numeric
association identifier, and it must match the partition the token was issued for. Routes that take an
`{id}` instead resolve the tenant from the record itself.

### Searching

Collection endpoints take an MSQL statement in `msql`, plus `page` (zero-based) and `pageSize`.
MSQL is MemberSuite's SQL-like query language, for example:

    SELECT ID, Name FROM Committee WHERE IsActive = true ORDER BY Name

A search returns only the fields the statement selects, not the full record. To discover the fields
and validation rules for a type, call its `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint.

### Creating and updating

* **POST** creates a record. Do **not** send `id` or `systemTimestamp` — either one makes the request
  fail with **409 Conflict**. Audit fields (`createdBy`, `createdDate`, `lastModifiedBy`,
  `lastModifiedDate`) are assigned by the server and ignored if supplied. A successful create returns
  **201** with the new `id` and a `Location` header.
* **PUT** replaces a record in full. Any field you omit is cleared, so read the record first and send
  it back with your changes applied. If you include `id` it must match the id in the URI.
* **DELETE** removes a record by id.

### Custom fields

Associations add their own fields to most objects, and those fields do **not** appear in the schemas
below - the schema shows the standard fields only. Send a custom field as a top-level property named
after the field itself, alongside the standard ones:

    { "name": "Finance Committee", "isActive": true, "MeetingRoom__c": "Boardroom" }

Call the object's `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint to discover which custom fields an association
has configured and what type each expects. A custom field of type Document or Image is sent under
`<FieldName>_Contents` instead, as an object carrying `filecontents` (base-64), `filename` and
`filetype`.

### Concurrency and caching

Endpoints that return a single record support conditional requests: send the `etag` from a previous
response back in `If-None-Match` and you will get **304** if nothing has changed. An update that
collides with someone else's change returns **409** — re-read the record and retry.

### Long-running requests

Send `Asynchronous: true` on a POST, PUT or DELETE to queue the work instead of waiting. The response
is **202 Accepted** with a `Location` header pointing at
`/{module}/v{version}/asyncstatus/{id}`, which you can poll for the outcome.

### Media types

Requests and responses are JSON with camel-cased property names. Ask for `application/hal+json` to
receive HATEOAS `_links` alongside each record.

get.summary: Reports the health and build of the Events REST service.
get.description:
Requires no access token, so it is safe to use as a load balancer health check. The response carries the
            running assembly version and its build timestamp, and lists the XML documentation files Swagger loaded its
            descriptions from - an empty list there means this deployment is publishing an undocumented API.

get.summary: Reports the outcome of an asynchronous operation.
get.description:
When a request is sent with an Asynchronous: true header the API answers 202 Accepted and a
            Location header pointing here. Poll this endpoint until it stops reporting Pending: once the
            work succeeds it answers 303 See Other with a Location header addressing the finished record,
            and if the work failed it answers 500 carrying the error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the queued operation, taken from the Location header of the 202 response.

303.description: The operation succeeded. The Location header addresses the resulting record.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No operation exists with that id.

500.description: The operation failed. The body carries the error.

            The price returned is the one that attendee would actually be charged: member pricing is applied
            where the attendee qualifies for it, tiered pricing where enableTieredPricing is set, and
            cross-sell linkage pricing where the pair names a linkedProductId. Nothing is ordered or
            reserved - this only quotes.

get.summary: Lists the events an entity has been invited to.
get.description:

            the association's invitation rules already applied - so it shows what a portal visitor should be
            offered, rather than every event on the calendar. This is the endpoint behind an event listing
            page. Use events/GetEventsByInviteeWithFilters when you also need to filter on custom
            criteria.

parameters.description: Earliest event date to include. Defaults to no lower bound.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of events to return per page.

parameters.name: startPosition
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first event to return.

parameters.name: eventCategoryId
parameters.description: Restricts the results to one event category.

parameters.name: featuredOnly
parameters.description: When true, returns only events flagged as featured.

parameters.description:

            widens the results to events the public may not see.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

            cannot express. The filter is read from the raw body, so send it as JSON with no wrapper object.
            Every other argument still travels in the query string.

parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first event to return.

parameters.name: eventCategoryId
parameters.description: Restricts the results to one event category.

parameters.name: featuredOnly
parameters.description: When true, returns only events flagged as featured.

parameters.name: consoleUser
parameters.description:
When true, evaluates visibility as a staff console user rather than a portal visitor, which
            widens the results to events the public may not see.

get.summary: Reports how many registration places remain for an event or session.
get.description:

            capacity of null means the event is uncapped, which is not the same as being full -
            treat null as "no limit", not zero. This endpoint allows anonymous access so a public registration
            page can show remaining places without a signed-in user. The count is a point-in-time reading and
            can be taken by another registrant before you use it.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Identifier of the event or session to measure.
